SCENE 02 · THE COGNITIVE REDUCTION

Cloud shouldn't start with infrastructure.

The traditional cloud journey forces developers to become full-time cloud architects just to run their application. Pilot inverts this paradigm by starting where you live: in your code.

The Pilot Paradigm: Application-First Architecture
Cognitive Overhead: ELIMINATED

THE CANONICAL REASONING MODEL

The Five Questions EgyKode Pilot Answers

QUESTION 01LOCAL-FIRST ANALYSIS
UNDERSTAND THE APPLICATION

What did I build?

Pilot analyzes the source code and deployment evidence to understand the application as real production workloads — identifying languages, frameworks, runtimes, services, dependencies, ports, health checks, build commands, background jobs, databases, queues, storage, and existing DevOps configuration.

Result
A verified picture of what the application actually is.
QUESTION 02PRODUCTION REQUIREMENTS
UNDERSTAND THE INTENT

What does it need to handle in production?

Pilot turns business and production requirements into explicit constraints — including expected traffic, concurrency, availability, latency, growth, budget, security, data requirements, disaster recovery, operational preferences, cloud, and region.

Result
A measurable definition of what the architecture must achieve.
QUESTION 03FEASIBILITY + OPTIMIZATION
FIND THE BEST-FIT ARCHITECTURE

What architecture should run it?

Pilot evaluates feasible architecture compositions against the application’s workloads, requirements, provider capabilities, organizational policies, and cost — eliminating impossible options first, then comparing the remaining choices across cost, performance, availability, security, scalability, and operational complexity.

Result
The best feasible architecture for the user’s actual requirements and budget — with the trade-offs and reasoning visible.
QUESTION 04CANONICAL BLUEPRINT + GENERATION
TURN THE DECISION INTO A SYSTEM

What exactly needs to exist?

Pilot converts the selected architecture into a canonical blueprint, then generates the infrastructure and operational artifacts required by that decision — including compute, networking, storage, databases, IAM, secrets, containers, Kubernetes or ECS resources, Terraform, CI/CD, security, observability, backups, documentation, and runtime configuration.

Result
One architecture decision translated into a complete, traceable Cloud DevOps project.
QUESTION 05VALIDATION + HUMAN CONTROL
PROVE IT BEFORE DELIVERY

Can I trust what Pilot created?

Pilot validates the exact reviewed project for structural correctness, infrastructure consistency, security, cross-file dependencies, cost/component alignment, and available external tool checks — then presents the changes for review and keeps delivery under explicit human approval.

Result
A validated, reviewable project that is ready to deliver — without hidden changes or unverified claims.

SCENE 11 · BROWNFIELD ADOPTION

Already have DevOps? Keep what works.

Pilot respects your existing codebase. It scans existing Dockerfiles, CI pipelines, and Terraform configurations — integrating with your current tooling rather than demanding a rewrite.

PRESERVE MODE

Maintain Multi-Stage Dockerfiles & Existing Scripts

Zero Silent Deletions

If your repository already has tuned Docker builds or custom start scripts, Pilot preserves them verbatim. It never needlessly replaces working engineering assets.

Enterprise Rule Invariant:Human Consent Mandatory for Every Modification
SCENE 12 · DETERMINISTIC SAFETY

When Pilot doesn't know, it doesn't guess.

Generative AI tools hallucinate broken startup commands and dangerous security flags. Pilot follows strict deterministic safety: it identifies what is missing, explains why it matters, and asks for one human decision.

SAFETY INQUIRY: 1 DECISION REQUIRED
RESOLVED & SAFE
KNOWN WITH 100% PROOF
Spring Boot 3.2 on JVM 21
Target Port 8080 declared in Dockerfile
Multi-stage build generates /app/roadmap-service.jar
CANNOT BE SAFELY INFERRED

Production JVM memory allocation flags and active Spring profile require human intent. Guessing memory limits risks OOM-kills in production.

Select production execution contract:
Decision recorded in Canonical BlueprintNo Model Decides the Plan
Zero Invented Prices

Costs come from a captured AWS rate snapshot or live AWS prices you refresh; unknown items are never treated as $0.

Zero Invented Secrets

Pilot never generates dummy passwords or fake API keys; it provisions AWS Secrets Manager placeholders.

Zero Hidden Changes

Every architectural modification is output as a readable diff in your PR branch.

Zero Silent Replacement

Existing Dockerfiles and CI scripts remain untouched unless explicitly flagged for replacement.

Zero Fake Validation

Checks that cannot be verified locally are never falsely marked as passed.

SCENE 15 · THE AI PHILOSOPHY

AI that helps. Rules that protect.

Pilot refuses to place your production uptime in the hands of an unconstrained generative chatbot. Deterministic software remains authoritative for infrastructure, pricing, and security; AI assists through explanation and critique.

Deterministic Rule Engine
AUTHORITATIVE

Absolute System Authority

Strict, typed algorithms govern every mathematical calculation, resource sizing formula, and security policy. No model decides any of them.

  • Regional cloud catalog pricing & budget caps
  • Strict dependency graph & capacity sizing
  • Least-privilege IAM with no wildcard actions
  • Validation of the exact files before delivery
AI Reasoning & Critique
ASSISTIVE ADVISOR

Cognitive Explanation & Investigation

AI inspects edge cases, explains technical trade-offs in plain language, and critiques legacy configurations to provide developer clarity.

  • Translates complex topology trade-offs into plain English
  • Investigates unusual custom build scripts & dependencies
  • Suggests architectural alternatives for team evaluation
  • AI is off by default; a local model keeps code on your machine
